summary_raw: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. title: Google ships four TPU variants in one year as it ramps up competition with Nvidia
summary_raw: Google is expanding its TPU 8 family with two specialized variants: the TPU 8tx keeps sensitive data encrypted even during processing, while the TPU 8i Max doubles compute power and memory by placing two chips on a single package. With nearly 100 external customers now on board, Google is increasingly positioning its in-house chips as an alternative to Nvidia's GPUs. title: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter AI chip export controls
summary_raw: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman US intelligence agencies classify as a suspected Chinese informant. The board has launched an independent investigation. The affair weakens Huang's lobbying efforts against stricter AI chip export controls, with a newly elected Democratic Congress poised to ramp up scrutiny of AI chip smuggling to China and push for tighter restrictions. title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate
summary_raw: Consciousness researchers Anil Seth, Ned Block, and Giulio Tononi argue in a Nature commentary that today's AI systems aren't conscious and won't become so on silicon hardware. They consider the assumption that consciousness depends on computation alone "fatally flawed" and warn against granting rights to AI systems. title: Is AI Now Good Enough To Cure Cancer? | YC Paper Club
summary_raw: This week’s Paper Club is all about AI for biology. The cost of sequencing has collapsed, which means biology now generates more data than anyone can mine, and the models are finally catching up. We cover how falling sequencing costs are turning cancer care into a per-patient data problem, what it takes to model a cell rather than a molecule, what a language model trained on DNA actually learns, and why in-context learning showed up in a genome model that nobody trained for it.
